title: MESI Cache Line Coherence FSM
constraints: Track one cache line's MESI state. Encoding: `state` = 0 Invalid, 1 Shared, 2 Exclusive, 3 Modified.

Exactly one of `pr_rd` (local read), `pr_wr` (local write), `bus_rd` (another cache reads this line) and `bus_rdx` (another cache wants it exclusively) is ever asserted in a cycle, or none of them. `shared_in` only matters together with `pr_rd`.

Transitions: `pr_rd` from Invalid goes to Exclusive, or to Shared if `shared_in = 1`; from Shared/Exclusive/Modified it has no effect. `pr_wr` always goes straight to Modified, from any state. `bus_rd` moves Exclusive to Shared and Modified to Shared; Invalid and Shared are unaffected. `bus_rdx` moves any state to Invalid.

`wb` (write-back) is a one-cycle pulse, asserted exactly when the *current* state is Modified and `bus_rd` or `bus_rdx` fires (the dirty line must be flushed before it can be shared or invalidated) — never on any other transition.
Synchronous reset: `state` = Invalid (0), `wb` = 0. All outputs are registered. Must be synthesizable.
hints: This is exactly the textbook 4-state MESI diagram: work out the four rows (one per current state) for the four possible triggers, then it's a straightforward case statement.
`wb` only depends on the state you're leaving and which bus signal fired — it does not depend on where you're going.
Only Modified is dirty. A cache line that is Shared or Exclusive was never written locally by *this* cache without going through Modified first, so it never needs a write-back.

examples.check: Invalid + local read, not shared -> Exclusive
